items.title: Live: Trump touts 'swift, overwhelming' victories in Iran in national address
items.description: US President Donald Trump is giving a national address on the Iran war. Follow live.

items.title: Travellers 'take the plunge' with cheap flights via Middle East despite warnings
items.description: Australians are choosing cheaper airfares over safer flights to get to Europe by transiting through the Middle East, despite federal government warnings.

items.title: Donald Trump threatens to hit Iran 'extremely hard' over next few weeks
items.description: In his first national address since the start of the war, President Donald Trump says the US will hit Iran hard over the next two to three weeks, and tells allies they need to secure the Strait of Hormuz if they want to calm oil markets.

items.title: Australia to attend global meeting on Strait of Hormuz — without the US
items.description: Australia will join a virtual meeting of 35 countries to discuss plans to reopen and secure the Strait of Hormuz, and ease the oil shock rocking global markets.

items.title: PM announces gambling ad ban in stadiums, during school pick-up
items.description: Gambling ads to be partially restricted on television and radio, with opt-out rules for online promotions and a ban in stadiums and on jerseys under reforms unveiled by Labor.

items.title: Breaking: Class action filed against Kmart alleges 'systemic' wage underpayment
items.description: Kmart managers have alleged they were routinely required to work "well beyond" their rostered hours without receiving overtime rates, penalty rates, or prescribed allowances.

items.title: States and territories agree to extra fuel excise cut using GST revenue
items.description: Premiers and chief ministers agree to use an estimated $400 million in extra GST revenue to fund a 5.7 per litre cut to the fuel excise, on top of the Commonwealth's 26.3 cent per litre relief.

items.title: Track the latest petrol and diesel prices around Australia
items.description: See what's happening with petrol and diesel prices near you, updated constantly.

items.title: Thousands lost to cancellations as fuel crisis bites southern Qld tourism sector
items.description: Tourism businesses say they’re bearing the brunt of surging fuel prices, with some losing thousands to booking cancellations and extra operational costs, while others field back-to-back calls from anxious tourists about fuel availability.

items.title: In pictures: Artemis II NASA's first mission to the Moon in decades
items.description: For the first time in more than 50 years NASA has sent astronauts around the Moon, marking a major milestone in a new era of space exploration.

items.title: Sit back and let us take you to the Moon with Artemis II
items.description: If all goes well for NASA's mission, the astronauts aboard could fly the furthest that humans have ever gone. What should we be looking out for?

items.title: Live: ASX unimpressed by Trump speech
items.description: ASX drops back following President Donald Trump's speech on Iran. Follow the day's events and insights from our business reporters on the ABC News live markets blog.

items.title: Bondi gunman fails to have family's identities suppressed for 40 years
items.description: Lawyers for Bondi gunman Naveed Akram fail in a bid to have the identities of his mother, brother and sister protected by a decades-long court suppression order on safety grounds.

items.title: 160-year-old historic stone cottage for sale for first time in decades
items.description: Originally built as storage for a grand residence, the stone cottage is the last surviving structure, going back to the very foundations of the city.

items.title: Here is the key to getting through The Super Mario Galaxy Movie
items.description: Even with downgraded expectations, the Nintendo sequel is little more than Easter eggs and bright colours. But that won't stop it from filling cinemas.

items.title: Museum fans: Test yourself with our curious collection of trivia
items.description: Australia’s museums hold a treasure trove of odd facts, native animals and even burlesque history. So how much do you know about the things hidden in our nation’s vaults?

items.title: Australian-based Harrods survivor was 'fresh game' for Mohamed Al Fayed
items.description: Jessica tried to keep her distance from Harrods billionaire owner Mohamed Al Fayed, who was known to abuse his female staff, until he spotted her going down an escalator.

items.title: Backpackers lose jobs in the wake of ex-Tropical Cyclone Narelle
items.description: In a WA town long reliant on backpackers, there may be few workers left by the time it is ready to reopen for business.

items.title: US burning through years' worth of critical weapons stockpiles in Iran
items.description: Analysts estimate the US is burning through high-end weapons in Iran at a rate that could take years to replenish, risking the West's military readiness for other potential conflicts.

items.title: Powerful magnitude-7.4 earthquake strikes Indonesia, tsunami warning issued
items.description: The quake, which hit early today, had a depth of 35 kilometres and its epicentre was 127km west-north-west of Ternate, Indonesia, the US Geological Survey said.

items.title: International crypto firm targets uni students despite ASIC ban
items.description: A major cryptocurrency platform is operating like "gambling" in Australia, according to experts, despite new regulatory laws.

items.title: DNA links US serial killer Ted Bundy to unsolved 1974 murder
items.description: New DNA testing definitively links infamous serial killer Ted Bundy to the unsolved death of a US teenager in 1974.

items.title: 'Domino effect': Why Singapore's oil shock will play out in Australia
items.description: Singapore is exposed to the oil shock from Iran's effective closure of the Strait of Hormuz, and its response will shape the fuel crisis in Australia.

items.title: What Australia can learn from French cities that made public transport free
items.description: There are growing calls in Australia for free public transport amid the Iran war with two states putting in place free services on a temporary basis. But in France, almost 50 cities have free public transport.

items.title: One Nation candidate published antisemitic, racist and homophobic posts
items.description: A One Nation candidate in the South Australian election was accused of domestic abuse, bullying and harassment, while another made racist, antisemitic and homophobic social media posts, raising fresh questions about the party's vetting processes as it surges in popularity.
